newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France cargo hit if strike starts.
newsitem.headline: Air France cargo hit if strike starts.

text.p: A threatened four-day strike by Air France pilots beginning on March 23 would have serious consequences on passenger traffic, while freight operations -- accounting for around 20 percent of global turnover -- will also be badly hit, industry sources said.
In 1996, Air France accounted for 55.5 percent of global volume of airfreight handled at Paris-CDG and Paris-Orly airports, totalling 1.1 million tonnes, Paris airport authority figures show.
The majority of Air France's cargo traffic -- around 55 percent -- is transported by its Boeing 747-200 freighter fleet.
Earlier this week, Air France brought an additional Boeing 747-200F into service, taking the fleet size to 12 aircraft.

Air France has said it was planning 35,000 flying hours for its freighter fleet during the summer season, which runs until end-October 1997, an increase of 14 percent on the same period last year. The airline recorded a 6.7 percent increase in cargo traffic in February 1997, with 390 million freight tonne kilometres (FTK).
In the first 11 months of its current financial year, which runs from April 1, 1996 to March 31 1997 -- Air France transported 4.41 billion FTK, up six percent on April 1995-February 1996.
Air France pilots have called a strike for March 23 to 26, as well as a possible further stoppage for end-April.
The strike was called in protest against the planned recruitment of 450 younger pilots, who would join on a lower pay scale.

Air France chairman, Christian Blanc, said the four-day strike was "indefensible (and) will have a cataclysmic economic and commercial effect on the company and will cost more than one billion francs, ($180 million).

A spokesman for one of the major pilots' unions at Air France (SNPL) said its members were split roughly fifty-fifty on carrying the strike through and it was impossible to forecast the result of a vote scheduled to be taken tomorrow afternoon.

The last major strike at Air France in October 1993 cost the airline around one billion francs in lost revenue -- 600 million francs in lost passenger traffic during 12 strike days and 380 million francs for freight over a 19-day period. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
